A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FacLens research despite the changed title and organization. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, were readable and supported comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original factuality-prediction benchmarks, runtime measurements, transfer experiments, ablations, and a user evaluation with 15 volunteers and 328 queries.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and reports additional comparator and model evaluations, feature visualizations, and a human evaluation with 22 volunteers and 680 queries.

M1.justification: The probe, CE and MMD objectives, and question-aligned batching remain. The described dimension adapter changes: v1 Section 5.2 and Appendix I project lower-dimensional states to the higher dimension, whereas v2 Section 4.3 and Appendix H project target-domain states to the source dimension. These procedures differ when the source model has the smaller hidden dimension.

E1.justification: Both versions use PopQA, Entity Questions, and Natural Questions for factuality prediction, plus freely submitted demo questions. Qwen2 and the larger human-study sample change model configurations and sampling within this coverage, rather than introducing a distinct dataset, task, or participant population.

E2.justification: V2 Tables 1–2 add SAT Probe and LoRA, introducing attention-based probing and parameter-efficient fine-tuning comparisons relevant to FacLens's effectiveness and efficiency. SAT Probe is evaluated on PQ and EQ, while LoRA also covers NQ. INSIDE and SAPLMA were already evaluated in v1 Appendix E; their move into v2's main text is not a new comparator addition.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen2-1.5B configurations and changes mixture-domain training from three to four models. Demo training changes from an 80/20 random split across all three QA sources to PQ/EQ training and NQ validation. The human study reports 22 volunteers and 680 queries instead of 15 and 328, with revised rating definitions. The reported answer-length exclusion also changes from fewer than three characters to three or fewer, although retained dataset counts do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 removes v1's semantic-gap analysis, training-size sensitivity study, and matched-size dataset comparison (Section 4.4 and Appendices B/F). It adds t-SNE analysis of shared features and last-entity-token ablations. Kernel plots retain NQ comparisons and add Qwen2 transfers while dropping the displayed PQ/EQ curves. The case study is substantially revised, including removal of the earlier reasoning-failure examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or performance error bars. The label audit retains sampling of 20 negative examples per model/dataset combination. Larger audit totals and revised point summaries do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds Qwen2, SAT Probe, LoRA, and last-entity-token results while retaining the shared last-token FacLens scores and runtimes. Averaging results change rather than merely move: LLaMA2/PQ middle-layer FacLens (avg) is 86.6% in v1 Table 1 and 88.5% in v2 Table 4. Three-point human ratings change from 202/328 (61.6%) to 483/680 (71.0%) under revised settings, so this is not a directly comparable gain. The label-quality summary also changes from 95% negative-audit correctness to 97.0% estimated overall correctness, which are different quantities.

T1.justification: The mixture-distribution derivation and MMD/CE objectives remain mathematically equivalent. V2 removes v1's explicit strict inequality asserting better distance estimation with aligned batches (Equation 7), replacing it with a qualitative sampling rationale. It also drops the separate formal NFD problem statement. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain efficient prediction from hidden question representations, shared prediction patterns across LLMs, and unsupervised transfer using question-aligned batching. The rewritten abstract and contributions emphasize FacLens and its effectiveness more strongly, but do not establish a substantively different core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 removes the explanation of weaker generalization to unfamiliar question topics, the recommendation to prioritize specific fields, and the threshold-selection limitation. The failure discussion shifts from temporal and reasoning questions to periodic events. It adds the black-box access limitation and qualifications about Qwen2's preferred layers and weaker transfer between differently sized models. These substantially change the paper's account of applicability and failure conditions.

D1.justification: V2 Appendices D–E add LoRA target modules, rank 128, alpha 256, training settings, and hardware requirements, and explain the MLP/CE implementation used for SAT Probe. V2 also specifies 12 Self-Evaluation epochs and discloses chat-template inclusion in question representations. Most FacLens architecture and optimization details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises positioning around representation engineering, entity representations, and attention-based factuality prediction, adding discussion of RepE, KEEN, TruthX, SAT Probe, and LoRA, among others. It removes the earlier open-world-learning literature tied to topic generalization. These are substantive literature and positioning changes beyond the switch to author–year citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and related work are extensively rewritten. V1's separate within-LLM and cross-LLM investigations become Preliminary, Methodology, and Experiments sections in v2. Human evaluation receives its own subsection, and the appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, adds t-SNE and labeling-process diagrams, expands tables and heatmaps for additional models and comparisons, and moves the post-hoc comparison into the main text. Averaging results receive a separate appendix table, and the two case tables become annotated example boxes. The document template and heading layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: The added LoRA and SAT Probe comparisons and smaller-model transfer tests strengthen evidence concerning efficiency and transferability. However, v2 removes informative generalization controls, training-size analysis, and threshold and reasoning limitations. Its revised human-study settings prevent interpreting the higher favorable-rating percentage as a direct improvement. These material gains and losses leave the net change in overall quality uncertain.
